notes:
This page numbers its own steps BY HAND as plain text ('1.' through '4.'), so the renderer's [N] markers landed on the wrong lines: [1] is the Zaffeld bullet, and [2], [3] and [4] are all route advice hanging off the hand-numbered steps. source_bullets therefore cites [N] only where a step really draws on one, and the page's own numbering is spelled out per step in its note; the last two steps have no [N] at all and carry an empty list rather than a borrowed number.

The two 'check' targets are real named entities -- Congregation Site and Rocky Outcrop both resolve -- so this quest gets markers where a page full of 'check the ???' would not. The Rocky Outcrop is visited twice with the Velkk hunt in between, which is exactly what the page says, so the repeat is kept rather than collapsed. Nothing in this quest is an item or key item, so there is no evidence anywhere and the ladder runs on the session latch; the '5 Velkk' count is likewise invisible. Bullets [2] and [3] are alternative routes into Cirdas Caverns, not steps, and are folded into step 2's note.

Fame 'akon' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only the raw string survives -- but FLevel 6 is real and is kept. Everything under bullet 2 is routing and a warning that Naji renders as if invisible; none of it is a step.

notes:
Bullet 1 is not a step: the quest flags ITSELF once the previous quest is done and Kieran has handed over the Ashen stratum abyssite III. That abyssite is earned in VW Op. 115, not here, so it is a precondition and can never be evidence for a step of this quest -- evidence has to be obtained at its own step. Start is left as the header's Kieran, since he is genuinely where the quest comes from, but the ladder opens on the battles.

The three Tier III Voidwatch fights are an unordered set in three different zones -- 'after defeating all 3' -- so they share a group and each keeps its own zone, exactly the case the guide calls out. Each zone lists three planar rift coordinates and the page does not say which one to use, so grid is null on all three and the coordinates live in the notes; picking one would be a guess. Nothing observable falls out of a Voidwatch win, so there is no evidence anywhere in this quest.

Bullet 3's sub-bullet is a real ordering constraint rather than trivia: Kieran must be spoken to before Gilgamesh or Gilgamesh's cutscene needs a zone first. That is why steps 4 and 5 are ordered and not a second group.

notes:
Two rungs on one moogle. Bullet 1 is a precondition -- zone after Glittering Gals -- and bullet 4 is the reward being described twice, once wrongly: it says you get the Morbol Mount item and its own sub-bullet corrects that to the key item Morbol companion. Neither is a step. The key item does not resolve against res/key_items.lua and the item Morbol Mount does not resolve either, but it makes no difference here: a reward proves the quest is over, not that a step is done, so nothing in this quest carries evidence and the ladder runs on the session latch across two steps at the same NPC.

The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is a version-update note and contains no steps. The reminder-text sub-bullet under bullet 2 is flavour. Where to buy Grow-M-Good is real advice and is kept as a note on the trade.

notes:
Bullet 2 is a heading -- 'Obtain a Rampaging Horn and a Lumbering Horn:' -- and bullets 3 and 4 are the two halves of it. The page imposes no order between them, so the two obtain steps share a group and each keeps its own zone and its own named ram.

The evidence sits on the LAST group member and is an AND-list over BOTH horns, following the same reasoning as the monuments in An Explorer's Footsteps. Putting Lumbering Horn on step 2 and Rampaging Horn on step 3 would look tidier and be wrong: whichever horn dropped first would advance the ladder past the group and point at Paujean while the player still had only one of the two. As written the ladder leaves the group exactly when both horns are in the bag.

Both horns also drop from unnamed BCNMs ('check the item page of the horn for details'), an alternative source the schema cannot express, so items_partial is set on both. Subjugation and the RoE objective under Bloodtear Baldurf are trivia. Fame is Norg, which IS one of the nine regions despite this being a Bastok quest.

notes:
The opening line -- 'Talk to Berghent near the Big Bridge in Western Adoulin (J-9) to start the Quest.' -- is plain text in the source, not a bullet, so the renderer never numbered it and [1] falls on Masad instead. It is unquestionably the first step, so it is recorded with an empty source_bullets and called out here.

Masad and Dewalt are the one real loss on this page. It names their buildings (the Mummers' Coalition and the Couriers' Coalition) but never says which half of Adoulin either building stands in, and Coalition halls are split across Western and Eastern Adoulin. Rather than guess a zone -- a wrong zone is a marker that never draws -- both steps carry a null zone, which matches wherever the NPC is actually found. Their names resolve, so the markers survive; only the zone narrowing is lost.

Step 5 is a harvesting point, which the page does not name, so the target is none. The Sickle is genuinely held equipment-as-consumable and is recorded in items; the page's warning to bring several is a note, because a count of spare sickles is not a requirement. The Blightberry is a key item (2386) and is the quest's only observable.

notes:
An eight-bullet ladder with no observable anywhere, and the page warns why: the quest never shows in the Current Log, so nothing reports even that it has been accepted. The one thing you are handed -- a Ducal Guard's lantern -- is a key item whose name is NOT unique in res/key_items.lua, so the resolver rejects it rather than guess an id, and it cannot be used as evidence. It is not an item either. That leaves the whole quest running on the session latch, which is the honest answer.

The four Braziers are one step, not four. They must be examined in a fixed order, none of them is observable, and a single 'Brazier' row in The Eldieme Necropolis draws all four at once -- four rungs the player cannot be tracked through would be noise, and the order is in the note where a player can read it. Note the zone needs its article to resolve: 'Eldieme Necropolis' does not, 'The Eldieme Necropolis' does.

'Quest Reqs: Bastok Mission 4-1 or San d'Oria Mission 4-1 or Windurst Mission 4-1' is a mission gate with no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it is flagged and gates nothing; only the header's Previous, Crest of Davoi, goes in prev. Bullet 7 says the reward, title and quest success all land at Baudin, and bullet 8 is still a real step after it.

notes:
'Level: 66+ Dancer' is BOTH gates -- level 66 and jobs ['DNC'] -- and 'Quest Reqs: Dancer level 66+' is the same sentence twice, not a second requirement.

Bullet 2 is an OR over two zones, 'Grauberg (S) or North Gustaberg (S)', and one step may only have one zone. It is split into two steps sharing a group. That is a slight abuse of the word 'group', which means an unordered AND elsewhere in this corpus, but it produces exactly the right behaviour here: both zones draw at once so the player can pick either, and the Dancer's Testimony hangs on the LAST member so that obtaining it -- in whichever zone -- carries the ladder past both at once. Putting the testimony on both would break the one-item-one-step rule. The wiki's '(S)' spelling resolves to the same zone ids as '[S]', so it is kept verbatim.

Bullets 3 and 4 are two separate trades of the SAME testimony: Laila takes it to teleport you and does not consume it, then the Burning Circle takes it to open the battlefield. Both therefore list it in items and neither can claim it as evidence, since it is already step 3's. Bullet 5 is the win condition -- Laila is beaten at roughly 25% HP rather than killed, and 'kill' is the nearest role the schema has. The After-the-walkthrough Notes section is about whether this quest is needed at all for the level cap and is not a step.

notes:
The header's giver survives contact with the walkthrough here, which is worth saying because it usually does not: two conversations come before Anteurephiaux, but bullet 3 states outright that HE is the one who 'officially' opens the quest, so start stays as written and Leporaitceau and Equette become steps 1 and 2. They are real actions the player must take, and prereq evaluation only runs for quests not yet started, so recording them costs nothing.

Bullets 4 and 5 are one place and are merged: 'travel to Misareaux Coast and look for a ??? at (K-12)' is how you get to the examine, not a separate rung. Bullet 6 is the reverse -- a fight and an examine in one sentence, 'once the NM is defeated, check the ??? again' -- so it is split into steps 5 and 6, the pattern the guide calls out with the leeches. The ??? keeps its rung and its zone but can never carry a marker.

The Whispering conch is key item 603, obtained at step 6 and handed over at step 7, so it is step 6's evidence and step 7's held item. Bullet 8 -- Equette again -- is what actually completes the quest, after the return to Anteurephiaux; both are kept. Fame 'Other' gates nothing.
